title: Windmill Growth started with a $500-a-month LinkedIn service and now brings in about $118K a month
dek: It began by selling likes and comments on founders' LinkedIn posts, then sold the bigger job: writing the posts. Its MRR (monthly recurring revenue: what clients pay every month) is $119,347, read straight from Stripe.
pattern: Start with a small, cheap service, then sell the bigger one

cost_to_start.text: Not public. A podcast about the founder says it was 'fully bootstrapped' (no investors).
cost_to_start.label: Claimed

first_revenue.text: A payment page at pay.windmillgrowth.com was archived on May 15 2024, the same day TrustMRR lists as the founding date. The first public plan was $500 a month.
first_revenue.label: Wayback

first_customers.label: Wayback

phases.name: A cheap first offer
phases.story: Windmill started by promoting founders' LinkedIn posts. The founder wrote the post, and Windmill made sure it got lots of likes and comments fast, so LinkedIn showed it to more people. That cost $500 a month. Writing the posts for you (ghostwriting) was the bigger plan at $1,800 a month. Don't copy the likes part: paying for likes and comments can break a platform's rules and makes people trust the post less. The useful idea is the cheap first offer.
phases.lesson: Start with a small, cheap offer that's easy to say yes to, then offer more to the people who stay.

phases.name: Bigger plans for bigger clients
phases.story: By January 2025 the cheap plan was $650 a month and the top plans were $4,999 and $7,499, aimed at companies with $2M+ in yearly revenue. The homepage said 'Trusted by 100+ Founders and Executives' and '7 spots left for January'. A case studies page was archived in February 2025.
phases.lesson: Once a cheap offer works, add a bigger version for customers who can pay more.

phases.name: A free tool as bait
phases.story: In April 2025 a podcast said Windmill had gone from zero to '$1M+ ARR in under a year', fully bootstrapped. ARR means yearly recurring revenue. A free 'AI Profile Optimizer' for LinkedIn went live around March 2025, and by August it was the banner at the top of the homepage.
phases.lesson: A free tool that solves a tiny problem brings in people who might buy the big solution.

phases.name: Writing for Google too
phases.story: Windmill published dozens of guides like 'LinkedIn ghostwriter cost' and 'Best times to post on LinkedIn in 2026', the questions buyers type into Google. In April 2026 the homepage said it 'works with the top 0.1% of startup founders'. Monthly revenue stayed close to $100K.
phases.lesson: Write the answers to the exact questions your buyers search for.

phases.name: Steady growth, one main plan
phases.story: Revenue rose slowly from about $108K to $118K a month. The site now leads with 'Your LinkedIn brand. Without the AI accent.' and the most popular plan is $3,999 a month. It says it has worked with 185+ founders and keeps 30 on the books at a time.
phases.lesson: When everyone uses AI to write, sounding like a real person becomes the thing you sell.

checklist: Pick one small, cheap version of a service you could do this week, like editing 3 short videos for $20.
Write down the bigger version of that service you could offer to anyone who likes the small one.
Make a simple payment link (Stripe, PayPal or Gumroad) before you have a single customer. You need a parent or guardian to set this up if you're under 18.
Help one person grow their account for free for two weeks, and ask if you can share the before and after.
Build or share one free tool or template that solves a tiny problem for the people you want to sell to.
Write one post that answers a question your buyers type into Google, in your own words, not AI's.
